job.style: a diary entry or letter by a student

response.passage: Dear Diary, today my science teacher explained why we must be careful about what we eat. I used to think that because vegetable oil comes from plants, fried snacks were healthy, but she explained that deep-frying destroys nutrients and adds unhealthy fats. I also learned that sugar hides in many places. Even if a snack tastes spicy or sour, it often contains high amounts of added sugar. My friend Rohan thinks he is safe because he never adds sugar to his tea, but he forgets that the packaged biscuits and cold drinks he consumes are loaded with sugar. The teacher also warned us about fruit juice. While whole fruits provide essential fibre, juice is just a concentrated sugar solution that lacks the fibre of the original fruit. Finally, she clarified that diabetes is a metabolic condition caused by lifestyle and diet, not a contagious disease that spreads like a cold. It is shocking to realize how much we misunderstand about our daily food choices. I have decided to stop drinking sugary sodas and start eating whole fruits instead. It is time to take my health seriously before I develop long-term problems like obesity or heart issues.
response.summary: This diary entry reflects on common dietary misconceptions regarding fried snacks, hidden sugars, and fruit juice. It emphasizes the importance of understanding nutrition to prevent long-term health issues like diabetes.
